## TRA Timeline

#### Origination and IPO

- 2016-07-08: TRA executed between Array Technologies, Inc. (New Mexico) and Ron P. Corio in connection with the private acquisition of Array Technologies Patent Holdings Co., LLC, giving rise to a Section 1012 cost-basis step-up in acquired developed-technology assets.
- 2020-09-22: First public filing of the TRA text as Exhibit 10.3 to the initial S-1; prospectus discloses $25.3M of undiscounted expected future payments as of June 30, 2020.
- 2020-10-15: IPO priced at $22.00/share (424B4); TRA carried forward as inherited related-party obligation, accounted for as contingent consideration at fair value through earnings.

#### Cash payment phase

- 2025-02-26: FY2024 10-K records the first year of TRA cash payments ($1.427M), replacing IRS-settlement reductions as the carrying-value-reduction mechanism.

## Explanation

Array Technologies, Inc. executed the TRA on July 8, 2016 with Ron P. Corio, the sole pre-acquisition owner of Array Technologies Patent Holdings Co., LLC, in connection with the private acquisition that produced a Section 1012 cost-basis step-up in the acquired developed-technology assets (later amortized under Section 197). The contract obligates Array to pay 50% of cumulative net realized tax benefits attributable to that basis step-up plus an interest-like Additional Amount, an atypical sharing ratio relative to the 85% TRA mode. The TRA was carried as a related-party obligation through the October 2020 IPO and has remained in force through subsequent corporate events (2021 Blackstone preferred-stock investment, 2021 and 2025 convertible-notes issuances, 2021 STI Norland and 2024 APA Solar Racking acquisitions, multiple credit-agreement amendments), none of which modified it. The carrying value has moved between roughly $8M and $20M across 2020-2025, reduced first by IRS-settlement adjustments to the underlying basis and, beginning in 2024, by cash payments to the beneficiary. See `contract_log.md` for the full filing-by-filing record.
